messages.content: Suppose a sequence of polynomials B_n(x) converge pointwise to f(x) on [0, 1]. Does it follow that the B_n converge uniformly? Ensure that stop words constitute no more than 20% of the total words in your response.

message.content: No. Pointwise convergence fails to guarantee uniform convergence. Counterexample: let B_n(x) = x^n, a polynomial sequence on [0,1]. B_n → f pointwise, where f(0) = 0, f(1) = 1, f(x) = 0 for x ∈ (0,1). Yet sup_x |B_n(x) − f(x)| = 1 ∀n. The supremum never vanishes. Pointwise ≠ uniform.
